sampling_model.design: The structural input fixes the legal action catalogue and binary-rational costs and supplies a charged source oracle.  Each distinct protocol runs on fresh independent units, is queried once and cached, and may contribute any number of positive labelled slices to different concrete target branches without paying its action cost again.
sampling_model.units: Each SELECT draws one fresh unit independently from the target population, and the unit's potential responses are generated by one recursive finite-discrete SCM compatible with \(G\).
sampling_model.treatment: RAND actions replace the catalogued node mechanism for their affected children, while CTF-RAND actions deliver the specified counterfactual value only to their catalogued child subset; protocol legality also enforces precedence, conflicts, and at-most-once mechanism use.
sampling_model.overlap: For each record actually used, the exact support table must assign positive mass to its event \(H_{\mathrm{slice}}(S,\ell)\), making the displayed conditional-law denominator nonzero.  No positivity is imposed on an unused source cell or unused event, and measured ancestry remains a separate endpoint-or-fixed-value condition.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None is used.  The oracle returns an opaque complete-law handle and exact finite support; every query and response bit is charged to \(N_{\mathcal O}\).  The results optimize operational acceptance and do not numerically evaluate a scalar identifying functional.

body.tldr: Complete operational CTFIDU\({}^{+}\) acceptance is equivalent to choosing legal physical protocols whose explicitly enumerated success sets cover every concrete assignment/equality branch \(\Omega\).  This yields the exact identity \(\operatorname{Opt}_{\mathrm{sw}}=\min_{\cup K_{\mathrm{sw}}(S)=\Omega}\sum_S w(S)\), an exact \(2^{O(m+L+\min\{M,2^m\})}\) optimizer, and a protocol-level \(H_M\)-approximation after at most \(2^m\) charged source-oracle queries.  Singleton ownership uses branch indices rather than dense masks.  Positivity is required only for slice events actually used.  The ordinary embedding is corrected to the finite all-cells \(Q[S]\) problem, so cost equality, NP-hardness, and logarithmic inapproximability transfer only on its explicit SELECT--RAND--READ image and stated oracle convention.

project_justification.gap: Fixed-source counterfactual identification does not choose among priced physical protocols, while prior ordinary design does not model CTF-RAND, reusable positive slices, precedence, conflicts, or assignment-dependent source switching.  Dense certificate enumeration also misses the induced protocol-to-branch cover structure.
project_justification.niche: The needed object is an operational, certificate-independent source interface together with a branch-indexed witness whose quantifier order remains \(\forall\alpha\exists\) and whose protocol costs are paid once.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies the switching normal form, the explicit coverage map \(K_{\mathrm{sw}}\), an exact weighted-cover identity, exact dynamic-programming or protocol-subset optimization, a protocol-level \(H_M\) greedy certificate, sparse branch-index ownership, a fixed-factor obstruction, and a corrected full-kernel ordinary cost equivalence.

body.related_work: Raghavan and Bareinboim (2025) provide the physical SELECT, RAND, CTF-RAND, and READ semantics and the CTF-REALIZE legality test; the present work prices collections of those protocols.  Raghavan and Bareinboim (2026) provide the fixed-source CTFIDU\({}^{+}\) recursion.  Here it is used only through the explicitly defined operational acceptance predicate: no semantic soundness or completeness extension to the larger event-local positivity class is claimed.  Correa, Lee, and Bareinboim (2021) motivate the unnested factorization, and Kivva et al. (2022) explain why positivity must be tracked, but positivity here is checked solely for used conditioning events.  Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash (2022, 2025) study the finite ordinary all-cells \(Q[S]\) design problem; the corrected two-way SELECT--RAND--READ embedding preserves optimum cost under the stated source-oracle representation convention and transfers their ordinary hardness boundary.  The \(H_M\) result here is a cover of complete legal protocols by concrete switching branches, not a global approximation for individual actions.  Park and Lee (2026) are a downstream counterfactual-bandit consumer, not a source of the acquisition theorem.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The branch count satisfies \(M\le k2^L\) and can be exponential, so the exact runtime and the sparse certificate may still be exponential.  Source support tables can also be exponential and every returned bit is charged to \(N_{\mathcal O}\).  The result is exact relative to \(\operatorname{Acc}_{\mathrm{sw}}\); it does not prove a new semantic CTFIDU\({}^{+}\) completeness theorem under event-local positivity.  General scalar lower certificates may be exponential.  The ordinary hardness transfer treats law/support access as an oracle response rather than expanding it into the polynomial structural reduction.
body.honest_scope: The proved primary claims are an operational switching normal form, an exact protocol-to-branch weighted-cover characterization, exact optimization and infeasibility at the stated exponential frontier, an \(H_M\) protocol-cover approximation, sparse branch-index ownership, and cost equivalence on the corrected finite full-kernel ordinary image.  Event-local positivity and measured ancestry remain explicit.  No scalar identifying functional, numerical evaluation, compactness theorem, conditional-query completeness, arbitrary partial-read completeness, mediator-depth fixed-parameter tractability, bounded-treewidth compiler, polynomial certificate bound, polynomial general lower certificate, or global action-cover approximation is claimed.  The older \(H_k\) action-cover result remains confined to its explicit one-action, protocolwise-legality, factorwise-no-synergy subclass.
body.interpretation: A physical protocol is valuable exactly for the concrete target branches in \(K_{\mathrm{sw}}(S)\).  Because slices of one acquired protocol are free to reuse, the planner pays \(w(S)\) once and covers every branch the protocol can certify.  The exact optimizer chooses a minimum-weight protocol cover and then emits one auditable positive, measured-ancestry source and restriction transcript for each branch.  Counterfactual structural causal bandits may use this certificate to compare acquisition plans for reward-distribution queries without requiring numerical evaluation of the reward law inside the optimizer.
